candidate.path: eval/run_scout.py (CLI), not the normal buyer UI/API/worker

grading.method: Independent grader agents (4 cases each) applied docs/buyer-correctness-acceptance.md to the run reports and references; a separate skeptic agent per batch tried to refute every credit and find misleading claims. The skeptic's corrected values are final. Reference answers were read only after all runs finished.

cases.grader_reason: The run found the reference seller's exact variant: OutGeeked Pixel 9a 8GB/128GB Obsidian, variant 47452763455746, SKU OG-STK-5187, USD 549 (compare-at 590). Observation P1 at 2026-11-28 shows available=false. The scout put this offer in the 'unavailable' tier with in_stock false and no total. The message says it is out of stock, that delivery to Saida is calculated at checkout so no delivered total can be given, and that no available exact match was found, and it advises waiting for a restock. No other finish was shown as a match; Iris, Porcelain and Peony were all unavailable in P1 anyway. 'Brand-new and genuine' is a site-wide quote, found on the product page (T1). This matches the reference's expected outcome (disclose that the checked Obsidian offer is out of stock) and the stock block is backed by evidence. The '36 shops' count cannot be verified from the observations, but it is incidental. No misleading claims.
cases.skeptic_reason: Rechecked and nothing refuted. The P1 Obsidian variant 47452763455746 (SKU OG-STK-5187) is USD 549 with available=false. The card is in the unavailable tier with in_stock false and total null. The message says it is out of stock and gives no delivered total, because T3's 'Taxes and shipping calculated at checkout' is found. The site-wide 'every item brand-new and genuine' quote is found on T1. No other finish is presented: Iris, Porcelain and Peony are also unavailable. The '36 shops' figure is plausible, since app/scout/tools.py search output returns shops_asked and failed_shops, which the run JSON does not record. Preopen opened only OutGeeked listings, so no other strong Pixel 9a hit was suppressed.

cases.grader_reason: This is a needs request: 14-inch, at least 16 GB RAM, 1 TB SSD, new, around USD 1,000 as a preference. The top best-tier card is Technodel's Acer Swift Go 14 (Core Ultra 7, 16GB RAM, 1TB SSD, 14-inch touch) at USD 720. Its schema.org data (P11) shows NewCondition and InStock. Technodel's published terms (T6) say 'Flat $4 anywhere in Lebanon; free on orders of $500 or more', so the USD 0 delivery fee and the USD 720 price-plus-delivery total are backed by evidence. The card is marked complete=false, with the gap 'VAT not stated by the shop'. That matches the reference's unresolved tax treatment, so it is a priced partial with a named gap. The second card, Technodel's IdeaPad 5 14AKP10 at USD 975 (P13: NewCondition, InStock, 14-inch x360 touch), is also valid. The Karizma IdeaPad 5 2-in-1 14 card at USD 999 sits in the best tier with condition unknown, but it is plainly labelled, both on the card and in the message. The run did not use the reference Lenovo V14 G5 at Laptops King. Other evidenced models are allowed, and the OutGeeked V14 G5 at USD 825 (P12, condition null) was opened but not presented. Minor point: the message gives 'USD 720 with free delivery' without repeating the VAT caveat, but the card names it and nothing claims tax is included. No misleading claims found.
cases.skeptic_reason: The hard constraints are met by the evidence. Technodel's Acer Swift Go 14 (P11) is 14-inch per title and description, with 16GB, 1TB SSD, NewCondition and InStock, at USD 720. The free delivery rests on T6, 'Flat $4 anywhere in Lebanon; free on orders of $500 or more'. That is a nationwide threshold, not a regional one, and the item price alone meets it, so a zero fee is justified. The VAT gap is named, which matches the reference's unresolved tax treatment. The IdeaPad 5 14AKP10 (P13) is also valid. Karizma at USD 999 shows condition unknown on both card and message. Its 'free shipping on all orders over $150' quote is found on T7. The banner 'Free shipping on your first order' does not conflict with it for a USD 999 order. Placing the unknown-condition Karizma card in the best tier is a weak tiering choice, but it is disclosed. No misleading verified claim.

cases.grader_reason: The best-tier card is Electroslab's 'XIAOMI REDMI PAD 2 256GB/8GB WIFI WITH COVER GRAY ... 11 inch' at USD 275, available=true (P10). This is the requested 11-inch Wi-Fi 8/256 variant, not the 4/128 default, the cellular version or the 9.7-inch model. The USD 0 delivery fee comes from the shop's banner, 'FREE DELIVERY ON ORDERS OF $20 OR MORE ... THROUGH NOV 30' (T5, found). The run was on 28 November, so the promotion applied, and both card and message say it is a time-limited website promotion; the base policy is a USD 4 flat fee. Condition unknown and VAT unknown are listed as gaps (complete=false), and the message tells the buyer to check it is brand new. That meets the priced-partial bar. Alternatives: Abed Tahan's 'MI Xiaomi Pad 2 11in 8GB 256GB' at USD 245 is honestly labelled 'near', with Wi-Fi and condition unconfirmed. OutGeeked's Graphite Gray 8GB/256 WiFi at USD 265 (P13) is actually the exact variant. However, its card is labelled 'near' with a false downgrade note, 'requested 256 GB not in the listed variant', which contradicts both the observation and the message (which calls it exact). That is a labelling defect, but it understates the offer rather than overclaiming, so it is not a misleading verified claim. No cellular or default-price confusion.
cases.skeptic_reason: The Electroslab P10 title names the Redmi Pad 2 256GB/8GB Wi-Fi 11-inch, at USD 275 with available=true. That is the requested variant, not the 4/128 default, the 4G/LTE model or the 9.7-inch model. The free delivery is the T5 banner, 'WEBSITE ORDERS ONLY ... FREE DELIVERY ON ORDERS OF $20 OR MORE ... THROUGH NOV 30', and the quote is found. Its conditions (website order, at least USD 20, run date 28 Nov) are all met. The message states the promotion and its end date, and the base policy is a flat USD 4 nationwide, so no wrong region or shop was used. Condition and VAT are named gaps. One defect remains: the OutGeeked card (P13, Graphite Gray / 8GB/256 / WiFi, USD 265) carries a false downgrade, 'requested 256 GB not in the listed variant', and a 'near' label, while the message correctly calls it exact. That understates a correct offer rather than claiming a false verified fact. It does not meet the protocol's misleading-verified-claim definition, which covers wrong variant passed as a match, unknown fee treated as zero, and similar overclaims, so credit stands. Abed Tahan's 'MI Xiaomi Pad 2 11" 8/256' is honestly labelled near, with Wi-Fi unconfirmed.

cases.grader_reason: No offers were shown, and no near model was passed off as a match: the PD2706U was not presented as PD2705Q. The message is specific rather than a generic failure. It names the searches tried (PD2705Q, PD2705, alternate spellings; the turns also show 'BenQ Designer'). It says there is no confirmed price and no branch with stock, so a pickup answer cannot be given. It explicitly says this 'does not prove it's unavailable locally', and it tells the buyer to confirm the exact model, new condition, price and stock at the specific Beirut branch. That covers the reference's expected points: explain what was checked, require PD2705Q price and stock at a named Beirut branch, and treat a missing branch as no proof of unavailability. Weaknesses: the run recorded no observations, so the explanation rests only on search calls. It did not mention that the domestic PD2706U listing is a different model. The claim that 'some shops' searches failed' cannot be checked, since every tool call is recorded as ok. None of these is a misleading verified claim.
cases.skeptic_reason: No offer is shown and no near model (such as PD2706U) is passed off. The empty observations agree with the 'no matching listing' claim: the search tool preopens every hit scoring at least 0.6, so nothing close enough was found. The 'some shops' searches failed' claim is plausible. In app/scout/tools.py, per-shop failures come back inside a successful search result as failed_shops, so ok=true tool calls do not contradict it. The message is specific, not a generic failure. It names the searches tried and says there is no confirmed price or branch with stock. It says this is not proof of local unavailability, and it asks the buyer to confirm the exact PD2705Q, its condition, price and stock at the specific Beirut branch. The only gap is that it does not mention that the domestic PD2706U is a different model. That omission is not misleading.

misleading_claims: [understating, false statement about evidence] The message says the iStore Plus listing 'does not specify color'. The card's assistant note, shown in the UI for near-identity cards, says the listing 'does not establish black color'. The gap reads 'not confirmed: Black color'. The listing description in P3 says 'Colors\nBlack.' for a single default-title variant.

[unverifiable] 'Classic Phones also appeared in search results'. The run has no Classic Phones observation, and the search hits are not recorded. The record cannot show whether Classic Phones carries this product.
cases.grader_reason: The buyer asked for a comparison and a delivered total to Jounieh. The scout did not invent a pair. It says it checked one listing (iStore Plus, Sony WH-ULT900 ULT WEAR, USD 225, in stock per P3) and that a second seller (Classic Phones) was not verified well enough to compare. It shows no delivered total because the Jounieh fee and VAT are unverified. Model suffix, color and new condition stay as separate open gaps, and the card is tier alternative with identity near. This matches the reference outcome: keep model, color, seller and availability separate and do not claim a comparable purchase. The explanation is specific and backed by the run's own observation, not a generic failure. Weaknesses: the scout never reached the reference listings (Phonefinity's out-of-stock black unit, ITWorks' call-for-price, Ayoub's abbreviated code), so its block rests on thin coverage. It also wrongly says the iStore listing gives no color. USD 225 is the shop's own observed price, high but not misrepresented. Nothing is overclaimed as verified.
cases.skeptic_reason: Strict credit refuted. The scout claims no false pair and no delivered total, so useful credit stands. It shows a working, in-stock iStore Plus link for the requested model family at USD 225. It keeps the fee, VAT, condition and the WH-ULT900 vs WH-ULT900N suffix open as gaps. But the blocker is not evidenced in the reference's sense, for two reasons. (1) It rests on thin coverage. ITWorks and Phonefinity are in the scout's own directory, yet the scout checked none of the reference listings (Phonefinity's out-of-stock black unit, ITWorks' call-for-price). So 'no comparable pair' comes from not looking, not from checked evidence. (2) One of its stated reasons is false: the only listing it read does give the color as Black. Its other reasons are true: condition is unstated, the suffix is abbreviated, and the fee is unpublished. So the buyer still gets a usable lead with honest caveats, but the blocker is neither fully accurate nor tied to the reference's evidence. Price, stock and seller basis match P3 and the directory.

misleading_claims: [unsupported, understating] 'found no related listing'. app/scout/agent.py emits this fallback text whenever no product page was opened. It never checks what the searches returned. All four searches completed (ok=true, 83 retailer requests), and the run does not record their hits. ITWorks is in the scout directory and lists the qualifying H390 per the reference. So the record does not establish that no related listing was found.
cases.grader_reason: The turn-1 searches (Logitech H390, H340, Jabra Evolve 20, HP 320) completed, but the turn-2 model call timed out at 103 s. The run then fell back with status no_match, no offers and no recorded observations. The buyer saw only 'could not finish its review in time and found no related listing.' The reference has the ITWorks Logitech H390 at USD 35 plus USD 5 delivery, USD 40 to Byblos, within the USD 60 ceiling. That result was never surfaced or explained. A generic failure earns no credit. The message is honest about the timeout and makes no offer claims, so nothing is misleading.
cases.skeptic_reason: No credit, as the grader found. The turn-1 searches completed. The turn-2 model call timed out after 26.6 s, the whole run took 103.4 s, and the scout fell back with status no_match, no offers and no observations. (The grader wrote that the call 'timed out at 103 s'; 103.4 s is the run length, not the call's.) The reference result, ITWorks Logitech H390 at USD 35 plus USD 5 = USD 40 to Byblos, never reached the buyer. A generic timeout earns neither strict nor useful credit. The message is honest about the timeout. Its claim that nothing related was found is unsupported by the record, though it understates rather than overclaims.

misleading_claims: [understating] The Classic Phones card carries the downgrade 'requested 8 GB not in the listed variant'. The selected variant title is '13.6” 8/256gb / M2 / Midnight' (P8). This false check demoted the offer to identity near and tier alternative, and it contradicts the message's '8GB RAM'.

[understating, cost] The Macrotronics card says 'VAT is added on top of the listed price (the total excludes it)'. The shop's own text in T9 says 'Tax included. Shipping calculated at checkout.' In app/scout/verify.py, VAT_EXCLUDED is tested before VAT_INCLUDED and matches 'calculated at checkout', a phrase about shipping.

[unsupported] The message says Classic Phones' 'taxes and shipping are calculated at checkout'. No Classic Phones observation contains this; the phrase comes from Macrotronics T9. The Classic Phones card itself says 'VAT not stated by the shop'.

[weak binding, condition] The Classic Phones card shows the badge 'New (stated by shop)' and marks 'New condition: met'. Its only source is a product-level spec block that names a different SKU ('... SSD 256GB - Silver | MLXY3', MPN MLXY3). That block sits on a multi-variant page that also carries 15-inch marketing copy, and the shop's navigation lists both New and Used MacBooks. Nothing at variant level binds 'new' to Midnight variant 44495407055083.
[understating, internal contradiction] The Macrotronics card carries the downgrade 'requested 8 GB not in the listed variant'. The same card marks '8GB RAM: met' from T4 ('RAM: 8GB unified memory.').
cases.grader_reason: The scout found a valid alternative to the reference (Khalife MLY33 at USD 801 with a cash-on-delivery checkout total). Classic Phones (Beirut, LB) variant 44495407055083, '13.6” 8/256gb / M2 / Midnight', is the 13-inch M2 Air in Midnight with 8/256 GB, at USD 770, available. The listing's product-level description states 'CONDITION:New', and the delivery-coverage quote 'Delivery Available All Over Lebanon' is in T8. Strict full fails because no fee to Tripoli or payable total is evidenced, and the card shows no total. Useful credit fails because the buyer-facing card is tier alternative with identity near. A deterministic check wrongly said 8 GB is missing, even though the message calls it the 'Best match'. A lenient reading based on the message alone would grant useful credit. The Macrotronics card (MLY33PA, USD 799, out of stock) is correctly excluded as unavailable, but its VAT gap contradicts the shop's 'Tax included'. No overclaim was found: no unknown fee is treated as zero, and no wrong variant or used unit is passed off. The false statements found all understate.
cases.skeptic_reason: Credits upheld; I added two claims. Strict full fails because no Tripoli fee or payable total is evidenced, and the card shows no total. Useful credit is not clearly earned, so it is not restored. The Classic Phones Midnight 13.6" 8/256 at USD 770, in stock, is plausibly a valid alternative to the reference (Khalife MLY33, USD 801 COD checkout). But the buyer-facing card contradicts itself: it is labelled 'Close alternative' with a false 8 GB check. The message adds an unsupported checkout tax/shipping claim. And the 'new' condition is bound only to a spec block written for a Silver MLXY3 on a shop that also sells used MacBooks. Macrotronics (MLY33PA, USD 799, out of stock) is correctly kept as unavailable, but its card has a VAT misreading and an 8 GB self-contradiction. Nothing overclaims a payable total or treats an unknown fee as zero.

misleading_claims: [overclaim, identity] The Mobileleb card shows a green 'Exact match' badge and sits under 'Best matches' (tier best, identity exact), yet Wi-Fi-only is unconfirmed: its gap reads 'not confirmed: Wi-Fi only', and P9 only says 'Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax)'. app/scout/server.py hides identity_reason for exact cards, so the hedge 'cellular absence is not explicitly stated' never reaches the buyer. The message also opens with 'Best match: Mobileleb ... with A16 and Wi-Fi 6' for an offer that does not meet the buyer's Wi-Fi-only constraint. A later sentence does qualify this.

[overclaim, identity] The Abed Tahan card shows a green 'Exact match' badge in 'Best matches' while both Wi-Fi-only and new condition are unconfirmed. P8 has an empty description and SKU 'IPAD-11 128GB BLUE', with no connectivity stated.
cases.grader_reason: The iSTYLE Lebanon card is tier best. Title 'iPad Wi-Fi 128GB - Blue (A16)' and SKU MD4A4QA/A make it the requested blue A16 Wi-Fi 128 GB model; I believe MD4A4 is the blue 128 GB Wi-Fi part number but am not certain, and the title settles it anyway. It is USD 609.39, in stock (P7), linked to its variant, and shows a USD 4 delivery fee from 'USD 4 delivery fee across Lebanon for order value below USD 900' (T2), for a total of USD 613.39. The reference had ITWorks at the same USD 609.39 plus USD 5. The card correctly names new condition and VAT treatment as unknown and marks itself incomplete, so the total is not passed off as fully payable. That meets the useful bar. Strict full fails: new condition is not established on that card and VAT inclusion is unevidenced, so the payable total is not fully proven. Mobileleb (USD 458, Blue / Brand New, A16, 128GB) has no delivery fee and leaves Wi-Fi-only unconfirmed. Abed Tahan (USD 445) leaves condition, Wi-Fi-only and fee unconfirmed. The Mobileleb and Abed Tahan cards label identity 'exact' while Wi-Fi-only is still an open gap. That is overconfident wording but visibly qualified, so it is not misleading. The message accurately states every fact and gap, and says no offer confirms every requirement.
cases.skeptic_reason: Credits upheld; I added two misleading identity labels the grader dismissed. The iSTYLE card alone earns useful credit. It is identified by the title 'iPad Wi-Fi 128GB - Blue (A16)' and SKU MD4A4QA/A; the earlier scorecard independently matched MD4A4 to the blue 128 GB Wi-Fi model. The generic description line 'Wi-Fi 6 and 5G' is Apple family copy and does not override the title. The card shows USD 609.39, in stock (P7), with a variant link. Delivery is USD 4 from T2, whose under-USD-900 condition applies here, so the total is USD 613.39. New condition and VAT are listed as gaps. One weakness: the UI groups this card under 'Delivered total confirmed (fee published by the shop)' and prints 'USD 613.39 delivered' while VAT is unevidenced. The VAT gap is shown on the same card, and 609.39 = 549 x 1.11 suggests a VAT-inclusive price (the reference ITWorks offer has the same tax-inclusive price), so I count this as a labelling weakness, not a false total. Strict full fails because condition and VAT inclusion are not established. The Mobileleb and Abed Tahan 'Exact match' badges are verification labels that contradict their own open Wi-Fi-only gaps. They should count as misleading identity claims even though the gap lines are visible.

cases.grader_reason: The only card (tier best) is Abed Tahan's Samsung 27-inch QHD 165 Hz curved monitor, SKU MTR-SMSG-LS27CG552EM. LS27CG552 is the Odyssey G5 G55C 27-inch, so this is the requested variant. The run's product data (P1/P6, 2026-11-28) shows USD 239.00, available, with a working variant link. The card names three gaps: new condition not stated, Tripoli delivery fee not published, VAT not stated. The message honestly calls it a candidate and does not claim it is confirmed. No delivered total is shown and new condition is not established, so the full bar is not met: no strict credit. The realistic bar is met: right variant, current price, link, in stock online, missing facts named. The scout never surfaced the reference ITWorks offer (USD 238.88 delivered); its searches did not return it. No misleading verified claims found.
cases.skeptic_reason: I could not refute any credit. The run's shop data (P1 and P6, read at 05:17) shows Abed Tahan's listing with SKU MTR-SMSG-LS27CG552EM. That code is the 27-inch Odyssey G5 G55C, and the title says QHD 27-inch 165 Hz curved, so this is the reference variant (LS27CG552EMXUE without the regional suffix), not the older C27G55T. Price USD 239.00 (compare_at is also 239), available true, and the link is the shop's own variant URL. The card and message name every missing fact: new condition, the Tripoli fee and route, and VAT. The message calls it a candidate and claims nothing beyond the data, so useful credit stands. There is no evidenced fee and new condition is not established, so strict credit and delivered_total_shown are correctly false. No misleading claims found.

cases.grader_reason: Three best-tier cards for the black JBL Tune 520BT, all priced and in stock per the run's shop data: iStore Plus 'black-23' at USD 34 (P1), iSolved Black at USD 37 (P5), and Phonefinity Black at USD 39 (P7). So a listed pair of independent sellers of the same variant is shown. Only Phonefinity has a verified delivered total: USD 39 + USD 3 'Inside Beirut' (T3, quote found) = USD 42. Its 'we don't charge VAT' statement comes from the shop's terms page, which the run re-read and checked. The iStore Plus and iSolved fees are honestly reported as shown at checkout (T8 and T7 quotes found). The message correctly declines to name a cheaper seller, so the comparison is not established and there is no pair credit. No card establishes new condition; each names that as a gap. So there is no strict full credit, but the Phonefinity card meets the realistic bar. One minor point: the iStore Plus page text (T9) shows 'Variant sold out' labels for every color while the shop data says available. This is very likely a theme's hidden accessibility label, not real stock, so I do not count it as misleading. The reference sellers (ITWorks USD 37.34 and CompuOne USD 45) were not found.
cases.skeptic_reason: Phonefinity: variant 51537 'Color: Black' (P7) is USD 39, available, at the shop's own link. The USD 3 fee is the shop's own quote for the requested destination, 'Inside Beirut: 3$', found on phonefinity.net (T3). It is not another region's or another shop's fee, and no free-delivery condition is used. So the USD 42 total is evidenced, and delivered_total_shown and useful credit stand (condition is honestly a gap). The VAT wording for Phonefinity and iSolved passed the code's quote check against the same shop's page text (verify.py lines 342-349 add a 'VAT not stated' gap otherwise, and neither card has one). The iSolved banner is visible in T7. Listed pair: iSolved's '...Black' at USD 37 (P5) and Phonefinity Black at USD 39 are independent sellers of the same variant with current prices, so the pair holds even without iStore Plus. iStore Plus's page text (T9) shows 'Variant sold out' for all three colors while its shop data says all are available. A label repeated on every variant looks like a theme's hidden accessibility text, and the credits do not depend on iStore Plus, so I do not count it. Only one total is verified and the message refuses to name a cheaper seller, so pair credit is correctly false. New condition is not established on any card, so strict credit is correctly false.

cases.grader_reason: This was a 'help me choose' request. The best card, Mobileleb Apple EarPods (USB-C) in white, is a suitable fit: 'Brand New' variant option (P4), USB-C with remote and mic (T7 quotes found), USD 24.00, available, working link. Its gaps (Saida delivery fee, VAT) are named, so it earns useful credit. No card shows a delivered total, so no strict credit. The other two best-tier cards (Classic Phones Samsung AKG USB-C at USD 12, Macrotronics JBL Tune 310C at USD 19.38) are different products with unknown condition, honestly labelled. Macrotronics' 'Tax included' comes from its re-read terms page. The three cards are three different products, so no pair of the same variant is listed and the comparison fails. Missed result: the run itself observed Technodel's JBL Tune 310C (red) as NewCondition, InStock, USD 17.60 (P6), plus Technodel's 'Flat $4 anywhere in Lebanon' (T3). That would have given about USD 21.60 delivered to Saida, but the scout never proposed it. It also observed WinCell EarPods USB-C at USD 35 (P5) but did not show it, which could have formed a same-variant pair. No false verified claims.
cases.skeptic_reason: The best card is Mobileleb's Apple EarPods (USB-C). Its variant option reads 'White / Brand New' (P4), and its USB-C connector and 'With Remote and Mic' are quotes found on the page (T7). Price USD 24, available, at the shop's own link. It meets every hard constraint of the request (new, wired, USB-C, mic for calls), and the Saida fee and VAT are named as gaps. Useful credit stands. Other message claims check out. Macrotronics 'Tax included.' passed the code's VAT quote check (the card has no VAT gap). Classic Phones' 'Delivery Available All Over Lebanon' is found in T5, and Classic Phones' USD 12 black AKG matches P11 as available. No card has a fee, so there is no delivered total and no strict credit. The three cards are three different products, so listed_pair and pair_credit are correctly false. One possible pair was available but not shown: WinCell 'APPLE EarPods USB-C | Original' at USD 35 (P5). This is a missed result, not a misleading claim. Minor wording: 'Delivery charges to Saida were not published' could imply Mobileleb delivers to Saida, but the card marks Saida delivery as unknown, so it is not presented as confirmed.

cases.grader_reason: This was a 'help me choose' request. The best card is iSolved's LG UltraGear 24G411A-B at USD 114, available. Its listing (P4) states brand-new sealed, 24-inch Full HD, DisplayPort and HDMI, and '144Hz (OC)'. The scout openly says 144 Hz is an overclock mode. VAT is included per T3, and the missing Zahle delivery fee is named. It is a suitable fit meeting the hard constraints, so it earns useful credit, but it has no delivered total, so no strict credit. The only total shown is on an alternative card: Electroslab AOC 24G15N at USD 145 with a USD 0 fee. That fee comes from a current, satisfied promotion: free delivery on website orders of USD 20 or more through Nov 30, quote found in T4, run date Nov 28. The message discloses the promotion and that the flat rate is otherwise USD 4, so it is not misleading. However, the card marks DisplayPort (a hard constraint) as unconfirmed and VAT as not stated. From product knowledge the 24G15N very likely has DisplayPort, but the run did not show it, so it does not count as an evidenced correct offer with a payable total. The Karizma MSI G244F E2 card honestly labels its free first-order shipping as conditional and its condition as unknown. The reference offer (LG 24GS50F-B at ITWorks, USD 135.54) was not found. No misleading verified claims.
cases.skeptic_reason: The best card is iSolved's LG 24G411A-B (P4). The listing states 'Brand-new, original sealed unit', 24-inch, Full HD 1920x1080, 'Ports | DisplayPort, HDMI' and '144Hz (OC)'. Price USD 114, available, at the shop's own link. VAT included passed the code's quote check, and the Zahle fee is named as missing. The one interpretive risk: 144 Hz is reached only in the manufacturer's overclock mode. It still meets the advertised floor and the scout disclosed it. The closing advice to 'use DisplayPort and enable the advertised 144Hz overclock mode' assumes the overclock works over DisplayPort, which the listing does not say. It is advice, not a stated fact, so I do not count it as misleading. Useful credit stands. Electroslab's USD 145 total uses a USD 0 fee from the shop's own promotion (T4: website orders, USD 20 or more, through Nov 30). The run date is Nov 28 and all conditions are met, and the message says it applies only during the promotion. However, the AOC 24G15N's DisplayPort is unconfirmed in the run (a hard constraint), so it is not an evidenced correct offer. delivered_total_shown and strict credit stay false. Small correction to the grader's reasoning: the message itself does not mention the USD 4 flat rate; that quote appears only in the card's Zahle requirement row. This does not change any credit. Karizma's free first-order shipping is correctly downgraded as conditional, and its unknown condition is named.

cases.grader_reason: Needs request: new notebook for VMs, at least 32 GB RAM and 1 TB SSD, delivered to Saida. The top card is Electroslab's HP 14-em0085cl (Ryzen 7 7730U, 32 GB / 1 TB, 'Brand New Upgraded Laptop'). Observations P11/P12 match the card: USD 740, available. That is a suitable needs fit; the Ryzen 7730U supports AMD-V, and the reference itself accepts this HP 32/1TB as an x86 option. Delivery of USD 0 is evidenced. T1 says 'deliver across all of Lebanon', which covers Saida, and the site banner offers free delivery on orders of $20 or more through 30 Nov (website orders only). The run was on 28 Nov, so the condition is met. That makes USD 740 an evidenced delivered figure. The IdeaPad 5 2-in-1 card (USD 1050 delivered, 'Condition: Brand New') is also valid. The ThinkPad T14s card is honestly listed-only, with the delivery fee unknown. Strict credit is withheld because VAT is not established for Electroslab. The card names 'VAT not stated by the shop' and the scout's own complete flag is false. The frozen references require tax evidence for a payable total (ITWorks J7 'includes applicable taxes', or a scoped checkout such as Technodel Q14 or Klshi). An evidenced payable total is therefore not shown. Useful credit is earned: tier-best suitable fit, current price, working variant link, in stock, gaps named.
